svg.text: Core entities + the API — four nouns, five endpoints
entities map 1:1 to tables and inform the API · implement every API endpoint and the FRs are done
Core entities (bullets first — schema comes later)
Ride
id · riderId · fare · eta · source · destination · status (fare_estimated → …)
Driver
id · metadata (car, plate, photo) · status: available | in_ride | offline | request_sent
Rider
id · metadata (location, payment) …
Location
driverId → (lat, lng) — the MOST UP-TO-DATE locations
only current positions live here; everything else lives in the primary DB
API — one FR at a time
POST /ride/fare-estimate
body: { source, destination } → { rideId, eta, price }
creates a PARTIAL Ride row (status fare_estimated)
PATCH /ride/{rideId}/request
async → 200/202, matching happens off-line
the < 1-min match-or-fail budget lives here
PUT /driver/location
body: { driverId, lat, lng } — every ~5 s from the app
get missed this one early? fine — API grows as you design
PATCH /ride/{rideId}/accept · PATCH /ride/{rideId}/update
accept: { accept: bool } → matched · update: { picked_up | dropped_off } → next lat/lng or null
identity comes from the JWT/session header — never from the body
Why no user IDs in the body?
a user could request a ride on someone else's behalf by putting that user's ID in the body. Session/JWT header only.
